story.title: A collection of plausible judgments can be inconsistent
paragraphs: DPO (direct preference optimization) assumes that each response has one latent reward, which implies a strict ordering of the responses to a prompt. Yet a model judging pairs separately can prefer A to B, B to C and C to A; each judgment looks plausible, but together they conflict.

Selecting pairs by confidence alone ignores where a comparison sits in this structure, keeping redundant preferences and missing those that explain a contradiction. ContraSolver treats the responses as a directed graph whose edges are preferences, so a directed cycle exposes a conflict that no single ranking can represent.

mechanism.title: Train on the evidence surrounding a contradiction
paragraphs: The algorithm first builds a maximum spanning tree of the strongest comparisons. A reverse pass examines the remaining edges from low to high confidence: an edge that closes a directed cycle is marked contradictory, and the edges on that cycle become candidate training pairs. A forward pass adds stronger edges that give a new ordering and skips those already implied by a path.
DPO then trains on these supporting (heuristic) edges, not on flipped contradictory ones, in the expectation that learning the reliable comparisons also corrects the weaker, inconsistent judgments.

Higher confidence is thus treated as stronger evidence. A confidently wrong judgment can enter the spanning tree, flag a correct comparison as contradictory and become a training pair, giving an order that is consistent but wrong.

evidence.title: Consistency improves, but it is not fully solved
paragraphs: Random and Max-Confidence selection (keep the most confident pairs) use as many pairs as ContraSolver, so the comparison isolates which pairs are chosen. On positive-sentiment generation, Llama-2-7b-chat reaches 87.2% with ContraSolver, 80.3% with Max-Confidence and 79.5% with random selection.

The graph analysis measures consistency directly: for both models and all four datasets, fewer training prompts have a cyclic preference graph after self-alignment, but many cycles remain. The analysis reuses the original responses on training prompts, so it does not test new responses.

Crucial correction: DPO trains E_h, not directly the reversed E_c set. v5 demo implements Algorithm 1 (Kruskal maximum spanning tree, reverse and forward loops, 0.51 edge threshold) on a five-response graph, mirrored in Python at build time; ties are broken by list position and every kept edge on a closed cycle is marked heuristic. All demo probabilities are illustrative. Table 4 measures fraction of training input graphs containing cycles, not number of cycles or test-set generalization.
